subject: Creative Arts
source: NaCCA Creative Arts Curriculum for Primary Schools, Basic 1–3 (September 2019)
accessibility: Read prompts and choices aloud when needed. Practical responses may use classroom materials, movement, speech or drawing.

indicators.statement: Think about the people who live in the local community and describe what you know about their history and their culture or way of life.
indicators.content_standard: B1.1.1.1 Generate ideas for artistic expression from people, culture, environment and topical issues.

skills.description: Identify the subject, artistic method and evidence in a work.
Study and describe in visual arts.
Use artistic evidence to explain a choice or improvement.

questions.stem: A child draws a local market. A seller passes a bowl of tomatoes to a buyer. What is this work about?
options: Keeping the playground clean
Saving water at school
A tree beside a school gate
Buying food at the market
questions.answer: Buying food at the market
hints: Identify the action or subject at the centre.
questions.explanation: The described action centres on buying food at the market.

questions.stem: A child draws a local market. A seller passes a bowl of tomatoes to a buyer. Which detail could a learner point out in the work?
options: Two hands meeting around a bowl
Thin branching lines next to straight bars
A straight band above a winding blue line
A wrapper just above an open bin
questions.answer: Two hands meeting around a bowl
hints: Look for a detail the example actually describes.
questions.explanation: The evidence in the example is two hands meeting around a bowl.

questions.stem: A child draws a local market. A seller passes a bowl of tomatoes to a buyer. Which method is used?
options: Drawing lines of different shapes
Rubbing a leaf and drawing the gate
Drawing people and bowls in crayon
Cutting and sticking paper shapes
questions.answer: Drawing people and bowls in crayon
hints: Think about how the parts were made or performed.
questions.explanation: The example uses drawing people and bowls in crayon to show buying food at the market.

questions.stem: Which can tell us about a community's history?
options: A story from a trusted elder
A date chosen at random
A made-up tale told as a fact
Tomorrow's weather guess
questions.answer: A story from a trusted elder
hints: Look for someone who knows the community's past.
questions.explanation: Look for someone who knows the community's past. A story from a trusted elder.

questions.stem: A pot has a wide mouth and two handles. What might its handles help a person do?
options: Make it deeper
Lift the pot
Close its mouth
Change its colour
questions.answer: Lift the pot
hints: Look at the way hands could hold it.
questions.explanation: Look at the way hands could hold it. Lift the pot.

questions.stem: A child draws a local market. A seller passes a bowl of tomatoes to a buyer. Which idea does the work suggest?
options: Turn a tap off after use
People exchange goods at the market
A living plant and a built gate share one place
Put used wrappers in the bin
questions.answer: People exchange goods at the market
hints: Connect the detail to the idea it expresses.
questions.explanation: The detail of two hands meeting around a bowl supports the idea that people exchange goods at the market.

questions.stem: A child draws a local market. A seller passes a bowl of tomatoes to a buyer. Which source would help the class check its account?

hints: Choose evidence about the actual subject.

questions.stem: What is the best way to find out why a maker chose a symbol?

questions.stem: Which question asks about an artist's method?
options: How far is the hall from the road?
What day will the class go home?
How did you put the parts of the work together?
Who opened the door for the visitors?

questions.stem: A child draws a local market. A seller passes a bowl of tomatoes to a buyer. Which change would make the main detail easier to recognise?

Leave a gap so the wrapper can be seen

Make the gate bars stand out beside the leaf

questions.stem: A pupil wants the viewer to see that a sale is happening. Which detail would help most?
options: All the bowls are stacked in an empty room.
One person passes a bowl as the other offers a coin.
The fruit is hidden behind a large wall.
The two people stand far apart with empty hands.

questions.explanation: A sale involves an exchange between people. One person passes a bowl as the other offers a coin.

questions.stem: A drawing shows tiny figures beside a large tree. Which part suggests the tree's size?

The figures are small beside it.
The paper has four corners.

hints: Compare the sizes within the picture.
questions.explanation: Compare the sizes within the picture. The figures are small beside it.

questions.stem: A learner says one example shows how everyone in a country lives. Which reply fits the evidence?
options: The biggest artwork always speaks for all communities.
Every artist in that country must share that one view.
It shows one view. Other communities may show different experiences.
A work made long ago shows exactly how everyone lives today.
questions.answer: It shows one view. Other communities may show different experiences.
hints: Consider how many people's experiences one example can represent.
questions.explanation: Consider how many people's experiences one example can represent. It shows one view. Other communities may show different experiences.

questions.stem: Which words describe a pattern you can see on cloth?

The maker was in a hurry.

questions.stem: A museum label gives a maker, a place and a date. What can you learn from it?

The hall has a large store cupboard.
The curtain should cost more.
The returning words were clear, but we needed a cue for our entrance.
questions.answer: The returning words were clear, but we needed a cue for our entrance.
hints: Consider what helped or hindered participation.
questions.explanation: Consider what helped or hindered participation. The returning words were clear, but we needed a cue for our entrance.

questions.stem: How can a group see whether its revision helped?
options: Show both versions and ask about the feature it changed
Assume the second version must be clearer
Count the pencils used and stop there
Give the old version a new title
questions.answer: Show both versions and ask about the feature it changed
hints: Look for evidence about the specific change.
questions.explanation: Look for evidence about the specific change. Show both versions and ask about the feature it changed.

questions.stem: A group sings well together but the words disappear under a shaker. What feedback fits?
options: Ask the audience to guess the missing words.
Change every singer's name in the programme.
Keep the group singing and soften the shaker under the words.
Add a louder shaker to cover the quiet words.
questions.answer: Keep the group singing and soften the shaker under the words.
hints: Identify a strength and a change to the balance.
questions.explanation: Identify a strength and a change to the balance. Keep the group singing and soften the shaker under the words.

questions.stem: Which statement gives evidence for a judgement?
options: It is best because I say so.
The maker is my friend, so it is perfect.
It must be important because its title is long.
The repeated detail drew my attention to the main idea.
questions.answer: The repeated detail drew my attention to the main idea.
hints: Look for a feature and its effect.
questions.explanation: Look for a feature and its effect. The repeated detail drew my attention to the main idea.

questions.stem: At a local gathering one singer calls a greeting. The circle answers with two claps. Review the example or a class work about a group greeting its guests. Describe one feature, say how it affects the work and suggest a change for the next version.
hints: Connect the detail to the idea it expresses.
questions.explanation: For example, connect two claps after the greeting to the idea that guests are welcome in the circle. Other supported choices are welcome.

criteria.description: Uses an agreed criterion and cites an observable detail.
Judges the effect of a particular feature and proposes a related change.
